memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Do not slaughter a cow or a sheep and its young on the same day'"
- Lev 22:28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A mother and her young were not to be killed on the same day. The
sacrifice could still happen - but not like that, not both at once.

There is no elaborate explanation given. God simply draws a line
against a particular kind of cruelty. Even where death was required by
the sacrificial system, needless harshness was forbidden.

This tells us something about God's character that we should not rush
past. Holiness and tenderness are not opposites in Him. The same God
who demanded a spotless offering also refused to allow gratuitous
cruelty to a mother animal.

Dear friend, we sometimes picture God as either soft or severe, as
though He must be one or the other. Scripture holds both together
perfectly. Paul writes of the kindness and the sternness of God (Rom
11:22). Micah tells us what the Lord requires: to act justly, to love
mercy, and to walk humbly with our God (Mic 6:8).

In Jesus we see the two joined in one Person. He drove out the money
changers with a whip of cords and He gathered children into His arms
in the same ministry.

Ask God to shape both in you - a firmness about truth and a real
tenderness toward the vulnerable.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I tend to picture God as only stern or only soft?
2. Where in my life am I harsh when I should be tender?
3. How can I show mercy to someone weaker than me this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are both holy and kind. Form in me a heart that loves truth
and shows mercy, just as I see in Jesus. Amen.
